He shook his fist in Parliament and called them all villains, over one line of paint.
You see, in the 1870s, British shipowners have a trick.
They over-insure an old, rotting ship and cram it with so much cargo it sits almost underwater.
If it floats, they get rich. If it sinks, they get even richer.
Then an MP, Samuel Plimsoll, has the simplest fix ever.
Paint a line on the hull. If the water's over the line, the ship doesn't sail.
The shipowners just laugh. "A line of paint? On my ship?"
And plenty of them sit in Parliament.
So when the government quietly drops the shipping bill, Plimsoll explodes.
He jumps up, shakes his fist, and yells, "I am determined to unmask the villains!"
The Speaker orders him to take it back. He refuses.
The papers print every word, and one crowd says, "If Mr Plimsoll is mad, he should bite a few more MPs!"
A year later, his line is the law.
But it gets weirder. The shipowners get to choose where to paint it.
It takes years more shouting to fix that.
Today it's on cargo ships worldwide.
And rubber gym shoes with a stripe around the sole? Named after it. Plimsolls.
